purpose: Independent follow-up literature screen for a reproducible Binance USDT-M, at-most-two-position successor after Alpha 015 was vetoed. This is an admission screen only: it does not inspect project return data, register an experiment, or alter any sealed protocol.

hard_filters: Binance USDT-M perpetual execution only, with at most two concurrent futures positions and planned leverage at or below one
fixed causal information set and reproducible decision-time source availability
fees, slippage, funding, interim mark-to-market and liquidation accounted for before a pass claim
economic mechanism independent of sealed failed or accumulating strategy families
no configuration search, post-hoc condition or unmodelled spot/cross-venue hedge
discarded_source_classes: vendor or anonymous backtest claims without an immutable method and raw-data provenance
event studies that document a mechanism but do not define a pre-data trading rule
historical results with winner concentration incompatible with the capital-preservation objective

candidates.name: EXECUTION_CONSTRAINED_AUTOTUNING
candidates.quality: Primary preprint. It explicitly models funding, slippage, strict t+1 execution and configuration-search fragility, while stating that it is alpha-agnostic and that its linear-cost simulations exclude market impact and capacity.
candidates.reason: It is evidence for preserving the project's cost, bias and audit controls, not evidence for a new directional signal. Its Bayesian selection workflow cannot be adopted as an alpha without a separately sealed full trial inventory before any return access.
candidates.retain: Keep as a governance reference only.

candidates.name: FIVE_MINUTE_VOLATILITY_SPIKE_TWELVE_HOUR_LONG
candidates.quality: Detailed practitioner research page, not an independently peer-reviewed or reproducibly archived primary dataset. It reports a single held-out positive estimate after costs but also reports that 85 percent of the profit came from ten days and that results are slippage-sensitive.
candidates.reason: The proposed payoff is a crash-rebound/shock-reversal trade, adjacent to the sealed mean-reversion and volatility-event families. Extreme day concentration conflicts with the current objective's concentration and capital-preservation requirements. Reconstructing its winner after seeing the report would also be outcome-following.
candidates.retain: Do not register or retune a volatility-spike successor from this result.

candidates.name: LIQUIDATION_CASCADE_DIRECTIONAL_SIGNAL
candidates.quality: Single-event empirical study of the October 2025 crash across Binance and Bybit. It documents futures/spot divergence and liquidity stress but does not provide a general pre-registered trading rule or a point-in-time historical liquidation-data contract.
candidates.reason: It supports the relevance of the currently accumulating liquidation-risk telemetry as a risk diagnostic. It cannot admit a directional alpha because its evidence is event-specific and historical liquidation availability/receipt time remains unverified.
candidates.retain: Do not alter the fixed telemetry trigger, threshold or validation boundary.

candidates.name: PERPETUAL_BASIS_AND_PRICE_VOLUME_FACTOR_SORTS
candidates.quality: Accepted academic research describing a perpetual-futures cost-of-carry framework and cross-sectional basis/price-volume predictor sorts.
candidates.reason: The evidence is cross-sectional factor sorting rather than a single or two-position USDT-M rule. Basis/funding exposure overlaps the sealed negative basis/carry families, and an implementable broad sort would violate the two-position limit.
candidates.retain: Use as theoretical context for cost and funding attribution only.

next_action: Keep live orders closed and continue the unchanged forward-only liquidation-risk telemetry campaign. A future candidate may be registered only after a distinct, reproducible two-position mechanism passes an admission screen before project return analysis.
